0.label: head_face_with_blades
0.description: The top of the drawn rim: a broad face with heavy lids and a tongue-like chin, flanked by upright leaf or blade shapes and zigzag bars, with figures in the compartment to its right.
0.iconography: The ojú ọpọ́n (Ẹ̀ṣù) face; the flanking blades may be leaves or knives — both belong to Ẹ̀ṣù's and Ògún's worlds.

1.label: lower_rim_plait_band
1.description: The whole bottom arc of the rim: a large figure-eight plait at the foot, with a fish or reptile head at its left.
1.iconography: Binding at the foot of the tray, opposite the face — the same head-and-plait axis as FoA_04-5583.

2.label: chameleon_with_coiled_tail_left
2.description: On the left rim, a creature with a diamond eye and cross-hatched body above a coiled knot of its tail.
2.iconography: A chameleon (or lizard) with a spiral tail, mirrored on the right rim — the creature that tested the new earth in Ife's creation story, and a coil in the ouroboros family.

3.label: figure_eight_plait
3.description: The central knot of the foot plait, inside #1.
3.iconography: See #1 — a tighter crop of the same plait.

4.label: small_figures_upper_left
4.description: In the upper-left compartment, two small figures — one crouching, one with a drum-like object — above a zigzag band.
4.iconography: Attendants or musicians near the head of the tray; compare the drummer on FoA_04-5583 (#5).

panel.title: Survey drawing of a round Ifá tray: face, chameleons and a plait at the foot
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a round opon Ifá
panel.summary: A drawing of a round tray with a hatched field, a broad face at the head, a large figure-eight plait at the foot, and on each side a cross-hatched creature with a diamond eye over a coiled tail. It closely matches the photographed Modakeke tray FoA_04-5583.

register_readings.reading: Head: the face between blade shapes; small figures to its left, kneeling and staff-holding figures to its right.
Sides: mirrored chameleons with coiled tails (the right one undetected).

panel.composition: Head–foot axis (face and plait) with mirrored creatures on the sides — identical in scheme to FoA_04-5583.
panel.narrative: Either a drawing of the Modakeke tray FoA_04-5583 or a twin from the same workshop: face, coiled creatures, figures and plait in the same places. Either way it confirms that the chameleon-and-plait scheme was a repeatable programme, not a one-off.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'. Its value is as evidence of a repeated workshop formula.
uncertainties: The match with FoA_04-5583 is visual; the face treatments differ in detail.
